question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.
Meenakshi sweeps the ball excellently when she ________ an off-spin delivery.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. gets.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The main clause "Meenakshi sweeps the ball excellently" is in the Simple Present Tense, describing a habitual action / general fact about her batting.

• Rule — Simple Present Tense in a habitual/general-truth sentence: when the main clause of a sentence describes a habitual action, the subordinate clause describing the accompanying circumstance must also be in the Simple Present Tense (V1/V5), not in the future, present perfect, or past tense.
◦ Structure: Subject + V1/V5(s/es with third person singular) + Object.

• Since "she" is third person singular, the verb "get" takes the -s form, giving "gets", which correctly matches the tense of "sweeps".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "will get" is incorrect because it is in the Simple Future Tense, which does not agree with the Simple Present Tense used in the main clause.

• Option 2: "has got" is incorrect because it is in the Present Perfect Tense, which suggests a completed action, not a repeated/habitual one.

• Option 3: "got" is incorrect because it is the Simple Past Tense form, which does not match the present-tense habitual context of the sentence.

NOTE

• In sentences expressing habitual actions, routines, or general truths (often signalled by adverbs like always, usually, every day, when/whenever), both clauses are normally kept in the Simple Present Tense.

• Common SSC trap: mixing tenses across the two clauses of a sentence, e.g. using future or past tense in a clause describing a habitual/general-truth action.

question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the underlined word.
Her mother always encouraged the idea of early marriage.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Discouraged.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The word "Encouraged" means gave support, confidence, or hope to someone/something; promoted an idea. (प्रोत्साहित किया)

• Its antonym "Discouraged" means to deter or dissuade someone from doing something; to dishearten or oppose an idea. (हतोत्साहित किया)
◦ Example: The teacher discouraged the students from copying in the exam.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "Motivated" (प्रेरित किया): to inspire someone to act — this is a synonym, not an antonym, of "encouraged".

• Option 2: "Supported" (समर्थन किया): to back or approve of something — again a synonym of "encouraged".

• Option 3: "Cheered" (उत्साहित किया): to encourage with shouts of approval — also a synonym, not the opposite, of "encouraged".

NOTE

• Other common antonym pairs of this type tested in SSC: Approve × Disapprove, Support × Oppose, Promote × Hinder, Inspire × Discourage.

• Always underline/identify the exact tested word first, then eliminate options that are synonyms (a very common distractor pattern in antonym questions).

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word.
Apathy
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Indifference.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The word "Apathy" means a complete lack of interest, enthusiasm, or concern about something. (उदासीनता)

• Its synonym "Indifference" means the state of having no particular interest or sympathy; unconcern. (उदासीनता / निरपेक्षता)
◦ Example: The low voter turnout reflected widespread apathy/indifference towards local politics.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "Empathy" (समानुभूति): the ability to understand and share the feelings of another — this is nearly opposite in spirit to apathy, not a synonym.

• Option 3: "Aversion" (घृणा/विरक्ति): a strong dislike or unwillingness towards something — this implies active dislike, whereas apathy implies an absence of feeling altogether.

• Option 4: "Hostility" (शत्रुता): open unfriendliness or opposition — again an active negative emotion, unlike the passive unconcern of apathy.

NOTE

• Do not confuse apathy (no feeling/interest) with antipathy (active dislike) — both are frequently used as distractors for one another in SSC vocabulary questions.

• Other synonyms of apathy: listlessness, detachment, unconcern, lethargy (in feeling).

question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.
To face the music
option_1: Not knowing the real chords in music
option_2: Barring the entire audiences view at a concert
option_3: Being challenged to a music competition
option_4: To bear the negative consequences of wrongful actions
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. To bear the negative consequences of wrongful actions.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "To face the music" means to accept criticism or punishment for something one has done, or to confront an unpleasant situation resulting from one's own actions. (अपने किए के परिणाम भुगतना)
◦ Example: After the fraud was discovered, the manager had to face the music before the board of directors.

• The idiom is believed to have originated either from theatre, where a nervous actor had to "face" the orchestra (the music) while performing before an audience, or from military tradition, where a disgraced soldier was drummed out of his regiment to the beat of music.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "Not knowing the real chords in music" — this is a literal, unrelated meaning and has nothing to do with the idiomatic sense.

• Option 2: "Barring the entire audiences view at a concert" — this is also a literal and irrelevant description, not the idiomatic meaning.

• Option 3: "Being challenged to a music competition" — this incorrectly takes the idiom literally as relating to an actual musical contest.

NOTE

• Other common SSC idioms about consequences/accountability: "To pay the piper" (to bear the cost of something), "To reap what you sow" (to face the results of one's own actions), "To be in hot water" (to be in trouble).

• Do not be misled by idioms that literally mention concrete nouns (like "music", "horse", "cart") — their figurative meaning is usually unrelated to the literal words.

question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in active voice.
The new building was being constructed by the construction workers.
option_1: The construction workers were constructing the new building.
option_2: The construction workers had been constructing the new building.
option_3: The new building has being constructed by the construction workers?
option_4: The new building is being constructed by the construction workers.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. The construction workers were constructing the new building.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The given sentence "The new building was being constructed by the construction workers" is in the Passive Voice, Past Continuous Tense.

• Rule — Past Continuous Tense:
◦ Passive: Object + was/were + being + V3 + by + Subject
◦ Active: Subject + was/were + V1 + ing + Object

• Applying the rule: the agent "the construction workers" (plural) becomes the subject, so the auxiliary is "were"; the past participle "constructed" is converted to its -ing form "constructing"; and "the new building" (the original subject) becomes the object.
◦ Active: The construction workers were constructing the new building.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 is incorrect because "had been constructing" is the active form of the Past Perfect Continuous Tense, not the Past Continuous Tense of the given sentence.

• Option 3 is incorrect because it keeps the sentence in the passive voice ("has being constructed") instead of converting it to active voice, and it is also grammatically faulty ("has being" is not a valid verb form) and wrongly punctuated as a question.

• Option 4 is incorrect because it remains in the passive voice, Present Continuous Tense ("is being constructed"), not the active voice of the original Past Continuous sentence.

NOTE

• When converting Passive to Active voice, always first identify the tense of the given sentence correctly, since each tense has its own fixed active/passive structure.

• Common trap: an option may look grammatically fine but represent the wrong tense, or may still be in the passive voice despite the question asking for active voice — always check both aspects.

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.
'Rapid' may be replaced by '________'.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Speedy.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The word "Rapid" means happening or moving very quickly; fast. (तेज़ / द्रुत)

• Its synonym "Speedy" means moving or happening quickly. (तेज़ / फुर्तीला)
◦ Example: The doctors wished him a speedy/rapid recovery after the surgery.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "Gradual" (क्रमिक): happening slowly, in stages, over a period of time — this is actually opposite in meaning to "rapid".

• Option 2: "Legitimate" (वैध): conforming to the law or to rules — unrelated in meaning to "rapid".

• Option 3: "Artistic" (कलात्मक): relating to or characteristic of art — also unrelated in meaning to "rapid".

NOTE

• Other synonyms of "rapid": swift, quick, fast, brisk, hasty.

• Do not confuse "rapid" with its antonym "gradual" — this pairing is a frequent distractor in SSC synonym/replacement questions.

question:
Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph.

A. He used to commit one theft a year on average. The stolen money lasted for the year.
B. He chose the house at Shotover Grange to commit his next burglary. He studied the design of the house carefully for a fortnight.
C. He found that the family had gone to London and the servants to the movie. He broke into the house one afternoon.
D. He hoped to get fifteen thousand pounds worth of jewels from the safe.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. ABCD.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A coherent paragraph must follow a logical chronological/cause-effect sequence: general habit → the plan for the specific burglary → the actual act of breaking in → the intended gain.

• Sentence A opens the paragraph by introducing the subject's general habit — committing one theft a year, establishing the background.

• Sentence B follows logically, narrowing down to his "next burglary" — choosing the house at Shotover Grange and studying its design.

• Sentence C continues the narrative, describing how he found the house empty and broke in — the natural next step after B's planning.

• Sentence D concludes by stating his motive/hope — the jewels he expected to steal from the safe, which fits as the final, culminating idea.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4 (ABCD).

Additional Information

• Option 1 (BCDA) is incorrect because it begins with the specific burglary (B) before establishing the general background (A), breaking the logical flow.

• Option 2 (DCBA) is incorrect because it starts with the motive/hope (D) before the burglary has even been planned (B) or carried out (C), reversing the natural sequence.

• Option 3 (BDAC) is incorrect because it places the hope for jewels (D) before the actual break-in (C) and separates it awkwardly from the introductory sentence (A).

NOTE

• In para-jumble questions, always look for the sentence that introduces the general subject/background — it is almost always the opening sentence.

• Look for logical connectors, pronouns, and chronological order (e.g., "his next burglary", "he found", "he hoped") to link sentences correctly.

question:
Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph.

A. Chronic infections such as typhoid, chickenpox and others, for example, are no longer feared.
B. A factor contributing to the rapid rise of the population in recent years has been the drop in the death rate.
C. Because of medical breakthroughs, the death rate has decreased.
D. In 2001, the death rate in India was approximately 8.5 per thousand people.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. BDCA.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A coherent paragraph must move from the general topic sentence to supporting statistics, then to the reason, and finally to a specific example.

• Sentence B is the topic sentence — it introduces the main idea that the drop in death rate is a factor behind the rapid population rise.

• Sentence D follows logically by providing a concrete statistic — the actual death rate figure in India in 2001 — supporting the claim made in B.

• Sentence C then explains the reason behind this drop — medical breakthroughs.

• Sentence A concludes with a specific example of these medical breakthroughs — chronic infections like typhoid and chickenpox no longer being feared.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1 (BDCA).

Additional Information

• Option 2 (DBCA) is incorrect because it opens with a statistic (D) before the topic sentence (B) that gives that statistic its context.

• Option 3 (CDAB) is incorrect because it starts with the reason (C) before the main topic/claim (B) has even been introduced.

• Option 4 (ADBC) is incorrect because it opens with a specific example (A) before the general topic sentence (B), reversing the general-to-specific structure.

NOTE

• In para-jumbles built around a claim + statistic + reason + example structure, always identify the broadest, most general statement first — it is usually the topic sentence and the correct opening.

• Words like "for example" in sentence A are a strong clue that it must follow, not precede, the statement it illustrates.

question:
Select the word which means the same as the group of words underlined in the given sentence.
Manisha is a believer of fate.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Fatalist.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The phrase "believer of fate" describes a person who believes that all events are predetermined and cannot be changed by human effort. (भाग्यवादी)

• The one-word substitute "Fatalist" means a person who believes in fate and accepts events as inevitable. (भाग्य में विश्वास रखने वाला व्यक्ति)
◦ Example: Being a fatalist, he never worried about the outcome of his exams, believing everything was destined.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "Minimalist" (न्यूनतमवादी): a person who favours a minimum of resources or a simple style — unrelated to belief in fate.

• Option 2: "Socialist" (समाजवादी): a person who believes in socialism, an economic/political system of collective ownership — unrelated to fate.

• Option 4: "Catalyst" (उत्प्रेरक): a person or thing that causes or speeds up a change or event — this refers to causing change, the opposite idea of passively accepting fate.

NOTE

• Other common one-word substitutions for beliefs: Atheist (does not believe in God), Agnostic (believes existence of God cannot be known), Optimist (expects the best), Pessimist (expects the worst).

• Always match the underlined phrase's core meaning (here, "belief in fate") to the option, rather than being distracted by superficially similar-sounding words like "Catalyst".

question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice.
Dr. Joyce is studying an experiment in his laboratory.
option_1: An experiment is studied by Dr. Joyce in his laboratory.
option_2: An experiment was being studied by Dr. Joyce in his laboratory.
option_3: An experiment is being studied by Dr. Joyce in his laboratory.
option_4: An experiment has been studied by Dr. Joyce in his laboratory.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. An experiment is being studied by Dr. Joyce in his laboratory.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence "Dr. Joyce is studying an experiment in his laboratory" is in the Active Voice, Present Continuous Tense.

• Rule — Present Continuous Tense:
◦ Active: Subject + is/am/are + V1 + ing + Object
◦ Passive: Object + is/am/are + being + V3 + by + Subject

• Applying the rule: the object "an experiment" becomes the subject; since it is singular, the auxiliary is "is", followed by "being"; the verb "study" becomes the past participle "studied"; and "Dr. Joyce" becomes the agent with "by".
◦ Passive: An experiment is being studied by Dr. Joyce in his laboratory.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 is incorrect because "is studied" is the passive of the Simple Present Tense, not the Present Continuous Tense of the original sentence.

• Option 2 is incorrect because "was being studied" is the passive of the Past Continuous Tense, which changes the time reference of the sentence.

• Option 4 is incorrect because "has been studied" is the passive of the Present Perfect Tense, indicating a completed action rather than an ongoing one.

NOTE

• The Present Continuous passive structure "is/am/are + being + V3" is a frequently tested pattern; students often confuse it with the Present Perfect passive "has/have + been + V3".

• Always identify both the tense and the number (singular/plural) of the new subject before selecting the auxiliary verb.

question:
Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don't find any error, mark 'No error' as your answer.

You can fool some of the people all the time, and all the people some of the time; but you cannot fool all the people all the time.
option_2: You can fool some of the people all the time
option_3: and all the people some of the time
option_4: but you cannot fool all the people all the time.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. No error.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The given sentence is a well-known, grammatically correct quotation (commonly attributed to Abraham Lincoln): "You can fool some of the people all the time, and all the people some of the time; but you cannot fool all the people all the time."

• On careful analysis, each segment of the sentence is grammatically sound — the subject-verb agreement ("You can fool"), the parallel structure of the two clauses joined by "and", and the contrasting clause joined by "but" are all correctly constructed.

• Since none of the three underlined/segmented parts contains a grammatical, structural, or usage error, the correct choice is "No error".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2: "You can fool some of the people all the time" is grammatically correct — the modal "can" is correctly followed by the base verb "fool", and the sentence structure is sound.

• Option 3: "and all the people some of the time" is grammatically correct — it correctly continues the parallel structure begun in the first clause, with the verb "fool" understood/elided.

• Option 4: "but you cannot fool all the people all the time." is grammatically correct — the contrasting conjunction "but" and the modal "cannot" are used appropriately to complete the sentence's meaning.

NOTE

• In error-spotting questions, always check for "No error" as a genuine possibility — SSC papers do include grammatically correct sentences to test whether candidates over-analyse.

• Famous quotations are sometimes used as error-spotting passages precisely because they are already grammatically polished; be extra cautious before flagging an error in such well-known lines.

question:
Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph.

A. There are 1.52 billion Aadhaar cards given to the whole population as of February 2019.
B. A financial inclusion programme called the Prime Minister's Jan Dhan Yojana (PMJDY) makes services like banking, remittance, and insurance accessible to every Indian at a reasonable price.
C. Under the acronym JAM—Jan Dhan Yojana for Financial Inclusion, Aadhaar Biometric Identification, and Mobile Telecommunications—India is on the verge of a social revolution.
D. Beneficiaries may open an account with no balance.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. CABD.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A coherent paragraph must move from the overarching theme, to supporting facts, to the specific programme, and finally to a concrete detail of that programme.

• Sentence C is the topic sentence — it introduces the umbrella concept JAM (Jan Dhan Yojana, Aadhaar, Mobile) and the claim that India is on the verge of a social revolution.

• Sentence A follows by providing supporting data about one component of JAM — the number of Aadhaar cards issued.

• Sentence B then introduces the second component in detail — the PMJDY financial inclusion programme and the services it provides.

• Sentence D concludes with a specific detail about PMJDY — that beneficiaries may open a zero-balance account.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3 (CABD).

Additional Information

• Option 1 (ABCD) is incorrect because it opens with a specific statistic about Aadhaar (A) before the topic sentence (C) has introduced the overall JAM concept.

• Option 2 (BCDA) is incorrect because it starts by detailing PMJDY (B) before the broader introductory idea (C) is established.

• Option 4 (DCBA) is incorrect because it begins with a minor supporting detail (D) about zero-balance accounts before any of the surrounding context (C, B, A) has been introduced.

NOTE

• When a paragraph names an acronym (like JAM) that is then elaborated in later sentences, the sentence introducing/explaining that acronym is almost always the topic sentence and the correct starting point.

• Look for sentences that logically expand on named components introduced earlier (here, Aadhaar and PMJDY are both parts of "JAM" introduced in C).

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word.
Diligent
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Careful.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The word "Diligent" means showing careful and persistent effort or work; hardworking and attentive to detail. (मेहनती / परिश्रमी)

• Among the given options, "Careful" is the closest in meaning, as it conveys the attentive, painstaking quality that diligence involves. (सावधान / सतर्क)
◦ Example: A diligent/careful student checks every answer before submitting the exam paper.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "Spiteful" (द्वेषपूर्ण): showing malice or a desire to hurt someone — unrelated in meaning to "diligent".

• Option 2: "Awful" (भयानक/बुरा): extremely unpleasant or bad — the opposite quality, unrelated to diligence.

• Option 3: "Faithful" (वफादार): loyal and steadfast — describes loyalty, not hardworking care/attentiveness, and is therefore not the best synonym.

NOTE

• Other synonyms of "diligent": industrious, hardworking, painstaking, assiduous, meticulous.

• Its antonym is "lazy" or "negligent" — a common antonym pairing tested in SSC vocabulary sections.

question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the underlined word.
They live in the apartment above ours.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Below.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The word "Above" means at a higher level or position than something else. (ऊपर)

• Its antonym "Below" means at a lower level or position than something else. (नीचे)
◦ Example: Our apartment is below theirs, on the ground floor.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "Over" is largely a synonym of "above" (indicating a higher position), not its opposite.

• Option 2: "After" relates to sequence or time, not vertical position, and is therefore not a valid opposite of "above".

• Option 3: "Upward" indicates movement or direction towards a higher point, which is consistent with, not opposite to, the meaning of "above".

NOTE

• Common spatial antonym pairs tested in SSC: Above × Below, Over × Under, Ahead × Behind, Inside × Outside.

• Be careful not to confuse position-based words (above/below) with direction-based words (upward/downward) or time-based words (before/after), as they are often placed together as distractors.

question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select 'No substitution'.
Many noticeable people were present at the function.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. notable.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The word "noticeable" means easily seen or observed; apparent — it describes something that draws visual or perceptual attention, not a person's importance or fame.

• The context of the sentence ("Many ___ people were present at the function") requires a word meaning important, distinguished, or eminent, which is expressed by the word "notable".
◦ Example: Many notable people, including the Chief Minister, attended the function.

• Rule: In such usage-based questions, the substituted word must fit the intended meaning of the sentence in context, not merely resemble the underlined word in spelling or sound.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "No substitution" is incorrect because "noticeable" is the wrong word choice here and must be replaced to convey the intended meaning of "important/distinguished".

• Option 2: "notworthy" is incorrect because it is not a standard English word (the correct word is "noteworthy", and even that would be a less natural fit than "notable" for describing people).

• Option 3: "celebrity" is incorrect because it is a noun (meaning a famous person), not an adjective, and so cannot grammatically modify the noun "people" in this position.

NOTE

• Commonly confused pairs in SSC substitution questions: noticeable (easily seen) vs. notable (important/distinguished) vs. noteworthy (deserving attention).

• Always check whether the underlined word's part of speech (adjective/noun/verb) matches what the sentence structurally requires — this quickly eliminates options like "celebrity" above.

question:
In the following sentence, four words are underlined, out of which one word is incorrectly spelt. Identify the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
The sovenir shops within the amusement parks do sell well because the visitors are mostly children and the shops keep a good stock of objects that children find fascinating.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. sovenir.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The correct spelling is "souvenir" — a thing kept as a reminder of a person, place, or event. (स्मृति चिन्ह)
◦ Example: She bought a small souvenir from the amusement park to remember her trip.

• Spelling key: SOU + VEN + IR. The word is borrowed from French, from souvenir meaning "to remember"; note the "ou" after the initial "s", which is the part most commonly dropped by mistake (as in the misspelling "sovenir").

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "fascinating" is correctly spelt — it means extremely interesting or attractive, from the verb "fascinate".

• Option 2: "visitors" is correctly spelt — the plural of "visitor", a person who visits a place.

• Option 3: "amusement" is correctly spelt — the state of finding something entertaining or funny, from the verb "amuse".

NOTE

• Other commonly misspelt French-origin words tested in SSC: restaurant, connoisseur, rendezvous, liaison, entrepreneur, questionnaire.

• When identifying incorrectly spelt words, silently sound out each word syllable by syllable and check for commonly dropped or transposed letters (here, the missing "u" in "sovenir").

question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.
Stir up a hornets' nest
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Provoke trouble.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "Stir up a hornets' nest" means to create a difficult, dangerous, or troublesome situation, often by provoking many people's anger at once. (मुसीबत मोल लेना / परेशानी खड़ी करना)
◦ Example: His comment about the new policy stirred up a hornets' nest among the employees.

• The idiom draws its imagery from literally disturbing a nest of hornets — aggressive stinging insects — which would swarm angrily and attack anyone responsible for disturbing them.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2: "Resist a fight" is incorrect because the idiom is about causing/provoking conflict, not resisting or avoiding one.

• Option 3: "Create doubts" is incorrect because the idiom refers to provoking trouble or hostility, not raising uncertainty or suspicion.

• Option 4: "Scare the birds" is incorrect because it takes the idiom literally and unrelatedly, confusing hornets (insects) with birds and missing the figurative sense entirely.

NOTE

• Other idioms about causing trouble often tested in SSC: "To open a can of worms" (to create a complicated problem), "To add fuel to the fire" (to worsen a situation), "To rock the boat" (to disturb a stable situation).

• Idioms involving animals/insects (hornets, cats, dogs, horses) rarely carry their literal meaning — always look for the commonly accepted figurative sense.

question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the underlined word in the given sentence.
Aditi is meticulous by nature.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. careless.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The word "Meticulous" means showing great attention to detail; very careful and precise. (अति सावधान / सूक्ष्म)

• Its antonym "Careless" means not giving sufficient attention or thought to avoiding harm or errors; negligent. (लापरवाह)
◦ Example: Unlike her meticulous sister, Radha is quite careless about checking her work.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "accurate" is a near-synonym of "meticulous", meaning free from error or exact — not its opposite.

• Option 2: "precise" is also a synonym of "meticulous", meaning marked by exactness — not its opposite.

• Option 4: "concise" means giving information clearly in few words — this relates to brevity, not carefulness, and is therefore not a true antonym of "meticulous".

NOTE

• Other synonyms of "meticulous": thorough, painstaking, scrupulous, fastidious.

• Common SSC trap: options that are synonyms (accurate, precise) are placed alongside the true antonym (careless) to test whether the candidate has correctly identified the antonym versus a synonym.

question:
Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph.

A. Swarms have wreaked havoc on crops and caused famines and mass migrations.
B. Since prehistoric times, locusts have caused plagues.
C. Traditional methods of control rely on the use of pesticides from the ground or the air, although biological control approaches are also making great strides.
D. Changes in agricultural practices and improved observation of areas where swarms tend to form have lately allowed control measures to be implemented at an earlier stage.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. BADC.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A coherent paragraph must move from the historical background of the problem, to its consequences, to modern developments, and finally to the traditional methods still in use.

• Sentence B is the topic sentence — it introduces the historical background that locusts have caused plagues since prehistoric times.

• Sentence A follows naturally by elaborating on the effects of these locust plagues — the havoc caused to crops, famines, and mass migrations.

• Sentence D then shifts to a more recent development — how changes in agricultural practices and better observation have allowed earlier control of swarms.

• Sentence C concludes by describing the current traditional and emerging methods of control (pesticides and biological approaches), which follows logically from the idea of "control measures" introduced in D.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2 (BADC).

Additional Information

• Option 1 (DCBA) is incorrect because it opens with a recent development (D) before the historical background (B) that establishes the topic of locust plagues.

• Option 3 (BDAC) is incorrect because it places the modern development about earlier control (D) before the description of the destructive effects of swarms (A), disrupting the logical cause-then-response order.

• Option 4 (ABDC) is incorrect because it begins with the consequence (A) before the historical background sentence (B) that the consequence follows from.

NOTE

• In para-jumbles about a historical phenomenon, the sentence establishing the time frame ("Since prehistoric times...") is almost always the correct opening sentence.

• Track cause-and-effect and chronological signal words ("since", "lately", "traditional") carefully to determine the logical sequence of ideas.

question: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Sieze.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The correct spelling is "Seize" — to take hold of something suddenly and forcibly; to take possession of by force or legal authority. (जब्त करना / पकड़ना)
◦ Example: The police managed to seize the stolen goods before the thief could escape.

• Spelling key: Seize follows the exception to the common "i before e except after c" rule — it is spelt with "ei", not "ie". The given option "Sieze" wrongly reverses this to "ie".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "Erase" is correctly spelt — meaning to rub out or remove something.

• Option 2: "Dredge" is correctly spelt — meaning to clean out the bed of a river/harbour by removing debris, or to sprinkle food with powder.

• Option 4: "North" is correctly spelt — the cardinal direction opposite to south.

NOTE

• Other common "ei" exception words often confused with "ie" spelling: weird, either, neither, leisure, protein, caffeine, forfeit.

• The traditional rule "i before e, except after c" (as in "believe" vs "receive") has several exceptions like "seize", which are frequently tested in SSC spelling questions.

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

The Digital Saksharta Abhiyan (DISHA) or National Digital Literacy Mission (NDLM) Scheme has been formulated to (1)_________ IT training to 52.5 lakh persons, including Anganwadi and ASHA workers and authorised ration dealers in all the States/UTs (2)_________ the country so that the non-IT literate citizens are (3)_________ to become IT literate so as to (4)_________ them to actively and effectively participate in the democratic and developmental process and also (5)_________ their livelihood.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank No.1.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. impart.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The blank requires a verb that collocates naturally with "IT training ... to 52.5 lakh persons". The verb "impart" means to give or convey (information, knowledge, or a skill) to someone, and collocates idiomatically with "training" and "knowledge".

• Rule — Collocation: in formal/official English, the fixed phrase is "to impart training/knowledge/education to someone"; this is a standard collocation frequently tested in SSC cloze passages.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "attribute" is incorrect because it means "to regard something as being caused by", which does not fit the context of giving training to people.

• Option 2: "attain" is incorrect because it means "to achieve or reach (a goal or level)"; here it is the training that must be given, not something the Scheme itself is trying to reach.

• Option 4: "affirm" is incorrect because it means "to state something as true", which is unrelated to the act of providing training.

NOTE

• Common verb-noun collocations tested in SSC cloze passages: impart training/knowledge, conduct a survey, achieve a target, provide assistance, extend cooperation.

• When solving cloze passages, always test each option by mentally inserting it and checking whether it forms a natural, idiomatic collocation with the surrounding words, not just whether it is a plausible synonym.

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

The Digital Saksharta Abhiyan (DISHA) or National Digital Literacy Mission (NDLM) Scheme has been formulated to (1)_________ IT training to 52.5 lakh persons, including Anganwadi and ASHA workers and authorised ration dealers in all the States/UTs (2)_________ the country so that the non-IT literate citizens are (3)_________ to become IT literate so as to (4)_________ them to actively and effectively participate in the democratic and developmental process and also (5)_________ their livelihood.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank No.2.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. across.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The blank requires a preposition that shows the training is being extended throughout/over the entire geographical spread of the States/UTs. "Across" means from one side to the other; extending over the whole area of, which correctly conveys nationwide coverage.

• Rule — Prepositions of extent/spread: "across the country" is the standard, idiomatic phrase used to indicate that something applies throughout an entire nation or region.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "among" is incorrect because it is used for a distribution or relationship involving three or more distinct, countable things (e.g., "among the States"), not for spreading over the whole country as a single area.

• Option 2: "within" is incorrect because it means "inside the limits or boundaries of", which does not convey the sense of nationwide spread intended here.

• Option 3: "between" is incorrect because it is conventionally used for exactly two things or a relationship involving two parties, not for the whole country.

NOTE

• Standard idiomatic phrases: "across the country/world" (nationwide/worldwide spread), "among the states" (distribution within a group of more than two), "between two states" (relationship involving exactly two).

• In cloze passages, prepositions are tested mainly through fixed idiomatic phrases rather than pure grammar rules — memorising common collocations like "across the country" is essential.

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

The Digital Saksharta Abhiyan (DISHA) or National Digital Literacy Mission (NDLM) Scheme has been formulated to (1)_________ IT training to 52.5 lakh persons, including Anganwadi and ASHA workers and authorised ration dealers in all the States/UTs (2)_________ the country so that the non-IT literate citizens are (3)_________ to become IT literate so as to (4)_________ them to actively and effectively participate in the democratic and developmental process and also (5)_________ their livelihood.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank No.3.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. trained.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The blank describes what happens to "non-IT literate citizens" so that they "become IT literate". The verb "trained" (from "train" — to teach a person a particular skill through instruction and practice) fits this context perfectly, since acquiring IT literacy is a skill gained through training.

• Rule — Contextual verb choice: the chosen verb must logically connect the subject (non-IT literate citizens) with the stated purpose ("to become IT literate") — training is the direct means by which literacy in a skill is achieved.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "included" is incorrect because merely "including" citizens does not logically lead to them "becoming IT literate" — inclusion alone does not impart a skill.

• Option 2: "made" is incorrect because it is vague and does not specifically convey the process of instruction implied by "become IT literate".

• Option 3: "ordered" is incorrect because it implies a command, which does not logically cause someone to become literate in IT.

NOTE

• This blank connects thematically with the earlier blank ("impart IT training") — cloze passages are often internally consistent, so earlier context can help confirm later blanks.

• In official/government scheme descriptions, verbs like "trained", "equipped", "skilled" are commonly used to describe citizens gaining a new competency.

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

The Digital Saksharta Abhiyan (DISHA) or National Digital Literacy Mission (NDLM) Scheme has been formulated to (1)_________ IT training to 52.5 lakh persons, including Anganwadi and ASHA workers and authorised ration dealers in all the States/UTs (2)_________ the country so that the non-IT literate citizens are (3)_________ to become IT literate so as to (4)_________ them to actively and effectively participate in the democratic and developmental process and also (5)_________ their livelihood.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank No.4.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. enable.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The blank fits the structure **"so as to ______ them to actively and effectively participate...". The verb "enable" means to give someone the authority, means, or ability to do something**, which correctly completes the infinitive structure "enable + object + to + verb".

• Rule — Verb pattern: "enable + someone + to do something" is a standard fixed grammatical pattern used to show that something makes an action possible for the object.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "enact" is incorrect because it means "to make (a bill or proposal) into law", which does not fit grammatically or logically with "them to actively participate".

• Option 2: "able" is incorrect because it is an adjective, not a verb, and cannot grammatically fill a verb slot in the sentence ("so as to able them" is ungrammatical).

• Option 4: "regard" is incorrect because it means "to consider or think of in a particular way", which does not fit the sense of empowering someone to participate.

NOTE

• Common confusion pair: "able" (adjective, used as "be able to") versus "enable" (verb, used as "enable someone to") — SSC frequently tests this distinction.

• Other similar causative verb patterns: allow someone to, permit someone to, empower someone to, help someone to.

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

The Digital Saksharta Abhiyan (DISHA) or National Digital Literacy Mission (NDLM) Scheme has been formulated to (1)_________ IT training to 52.5 lakh persons, including Anganwadi and ASHA workers and authorised ration dealers in all the States/UTs (2)_________ the country so that the non-IT literate citizens are (3)_________ to become IT literate so as to (4)_________ them to actively and effectively participate in the democratic and developmental process and also (5)_________ their livelihood.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank No.5.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. enhance.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The blank completes the phrase **"also ______ their livelihood". The verb "enhance" means to intensify, increase, or further improve the quality, value, or extent of something**, which fits naturally with "livelihood" — the scheme aims to improve citizens' means of earning a living through IT literacy.

• Rule — Contextual/collocational fit: the phrase "enhance one's livelihood" is a standard, idiomatic collocation used in describing the positive economic outcome of a skill-development or welfare scheme.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "present" is incorrect because as a verb it means "to give or show something formally", which does not logically combine with "their livelihood" in this context.

• Option 3: "engage" is incorrect because "engage their livelihood" is not idiomatic; "engage" normally takes objects like "people" or "attention", not "livelihood".

• Option 4: "train" is incorrect because "train their livelihood" is not meaningful; "train" collocates with people or skills, not with the abstract noun "livelihood".

NOTE

• Common collocations with "livelihood": enhance/improve/secure/earn/sustain a livelihood.

• In cloze passages describing government schemes, watch for verbs expressing positive outcomes (enhance, improve, boost, strengthen) as they usually pair correctly with abstract nouns like "livelihood", "economy", or "quality of life".
